points: The next earnings print will reveal whether Q2 2026 sustained Q1's $2.7B revenue and $29.2B gross booking value momentum and whether Q4 2026 guidance implies demand is still outpacing supply headwinds.

EU Regulation 2024/1028, live since May 20 2026, could show up in Q3 and Q4 results as higher host friction and compliance costs; the long case holds only if those costs stay below 5% of revenue and listings do not collapse.

Active listings in major U.S. metros are already down 10-21% (NYC -20.6%, Nashville -21.4%, LA/Phoenix/SF/Austin -10-12%), so the next print's host-supply commentary will signal whether Q4 2026 faces a real shortage or the worst is already priced in.

Idaho and Indiana short-term rental restrictions took effect July 1 2026, so Q3 and Q4 results may show added supply pressure in those states; limited impact would confirm regulation is manageable for the long thesis.
Marriott reports on Nov 2, 2026, and its Q4 demand and pricing outlook could either reinforce or weaken confidence in Airbnb's U.S. travel tailwind before Airbnb's own Q4 catalyst.

The Q4 2026 earnings release, likely in early 2027, will capture holiday travel and full-year guidance; strong Q4 gross booking value and EBITDA margin near Q1's 19% level would set up a constructive 2027.
If NYC listings rebound above 90% of pre-regulation levels in coming quarters, the biggest regulatory fear would fade and supply risk would ease, strengthening the long entry.
